Neurology · published research

Cognitive impairment

Several small MCI trials reported better cognitive-test scores after PBM than after sham, including a 93-person trial with a MoCA difference that persisted at three months. A combined TMS and PBM trial cannot isolate the effect of PBM.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Several small MCI trials reported better cognitive-test scores after PBM than after sham, including a 93-person trial with a MoCA difference that persisted at three months. A combined TMS and PBM trial cannot isolate the effect of PBM.

Summary of the Evidence

We identified 19 unique titles in the exact cognitive-impairment category: 10 human research reports, four mouse studies, three narrative reviews, one systematic review and one meta-analysis. Human reports include five randomized trials, four other controlled or non-randomized studies and one case series. Two Korean fNIRS prediction reports from 2024 and 2026 appear to use the same 43-person research program, so they are not evidence of two independent trials. The 2025 meta-analysis synthesizes trials from healthy and cognitively impaired populations rather than adding new participants to this indication (Zhu et al. 2025).

Human and clinical evidence

In a double-blind trial of 93 adults over 50 with mild cognitive impairment, transcranial PBM produced a larger MoCA increase than placebo at the end of treatment, and the difference was still present at the three-month follow-up. Serum BDNF also increased in the active group (de Oliveira et al. 2024). A separate randomized trial in 42 older women reported short-term gains in cognitive and attention tests after five treatment days. A 20-person pilot in MCI reported better global cognition and episodic memory with active treatment than sham, but its small sample makes the estimates imprecise (Rashidi-Ranjbar et al. 2026). One trial combined PBM with transcranial magnetic stimulation, so its better working-memory results cannot be attributed to PBM alone. The prediction papers analyze response patterns rather than independently testing clinical efficacy.

Animal evidence

Four mouse publications examine cognitive outcomes in models of aging, brain injury or related neurological stress. They report changes in memory tasks and biological markers, but these models do not establish benefit for people with MCI.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified in this exact category. Blood biomarkers and neuroimaging measures were collected within human or animal studies and are not separate laboratory cohorts.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Reported clinical protocols vary from a single transcranial session to repeated schedules lasting several weeks. Wavelengths include red visible light around 610 nm and near-infrared light around 810 or 850 nm. Some studies target the forehead or prefrontal region, while one small pilot applied light over neck blood vessels. Devices include laser and LED systems. The available records do not provide a consistent set of power, fluence and exposure details, and these application sites and schedules are not directly interchangeable.

Interpretation

The results support a possible short-term improvement in selected cognitive tests for some adults with MCI. They do not show that PBM preserves independent daily function or slows progression to dementia. Confidence is limited by small samples, overlapping research programs, differing protocols and the short duration of most controlled studies.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term cognitive-test improvement in adults with mild cognitive impairment receiving the studied transcranial protocols. Very low for durable improvement or slowing of cognitive decline.
Publications and records19 unique titles

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The rating reflects several small controlled MCI studies with positive test results, alongside studies that measured physiology or combined PBM with another treatment. The available follow-up is short and protocols differ. Larger independent sham-controlled trials should use prespecified cognitive tests, track daily function and follow participants for at least a year.
